rule: Interface patterns don't port across domains, even when the problem looks the same.
quote: Interface patterns don't port across domains — even when the surface-level problem looks the same.
fragment: Interface patterns don't port across domains
where: Copying VS Code's multi-pane layout for writers.
why: Developers navigate by location. Writers navigate by narrative.

rule: Understand the shape of the work before you design the interface.
quote: You have to understand the shape of the work before you design the interface.
fragment: understand the shape of the work before you design the interface
where: The first design looked right on paper and turned out too complex.
why: A tool someone lives in has to fit how they actually work.

rule: A pane is a role, not a container.
quote: The rule: The support pane informs.
fragment: The rule: The support pane informs
where: Deciding the left pane is always the chapter.
why: The chapter is the unit of work, so it always gets the same place.

rule: Design for the screen your users actually have.
quote: Two panes isn't a compromise. It's designing for reality.
fragment: Two panes isn't a compromise
where: Choosing two panes, because most writers don't have ultrawide monitors.
why: The ideal layout is useless on the screen people really own.

rule: Trust the feeling that a design is wrong, even before you can say why.
quote: What I couldn't see past was this feeling that the shape was wrong.
fragment: this feeling that the shape was wrong
where: Three weeks of knowing something was wrong before I knew how to fix it.
why: The reason usually shows up later. The feeling shows up first.

rule: The story is the truth. The document is just one expression of it.
quote: The story is the truth. The document is just one expression of it.
fragment: The story is the truth
where: When beats stopped living inside the prose.
why: Prose changes constantly, and the plot shouldn't break when it does.

rule: Structural decisions are permanent until someone decides otherwise.
quote: Structural story decisions are permanent until the writer decides otherwise.
fragment: Structural story decisions are permanent until the writer decides otherwise
where: When the editor's undo and the database disagreed.
why: The fix, addToHistory: false, made the database the only record of a story decision.

rule: A dead end can be a fork.
quote: The Ghost state is a fork, not a dead end.
fragment: is a fork, not a dead end
where: Ghost beats that lost their text.
why: A ghost beat can be re-anchored, so losing its text isn't losing the idea.

rule: Wild customization needs rigid primitives underneath.
quote: The revelation: to allow for wild, chaotic customization, you need absolute, rigid primitives underneath.
fragment: you need absolute, rigid primitives underneath
where: The navbar turning cream from a Tailwind v4 token collision.
why: Themes only work when components don't decide their own look.

rule: A component should know nothing about its own appearance.
quote: The component has to become entirely ignorant of its own appearance.
fragment: entirely ignorant of its own appearance
where: Building 19 strict UI primitives before more features.
why: Hardcoded styles were blocking the theme work I'd planned.

rule: Understand the trade-offs you're willing to make, then accept them.
quote: I traded aesthetic debt in a secondary feature to pay off the discovery debt blocking my primary feature.
fragment: I traded aesthetic debt
where: Leaving a panel ugly on purpose.
why: Every choice costs something. The mistake is not knowing what.

rule: Accept small visible progress when the invisible progress is enormous.
quote: It's accepting that the visible output will be small so the invisible progress can be enormous.
fragment: the invisible progress can be enormous
where: A month spent on primitives nobody would see.
why: The foundations don't show, but everything after stands on them.

rule: A story was never a line. The line is how we read it.
quote: A story was never a line. The line is how we read it.
fragment: A story was never a line
where: Moving from a linear outline to a graph of the story.
why: The shape of the tool should follow the shape of the thing, not the order we read it in.

rule: The system doesn't decide what matters. The writer does.
quote: The system doesn't decide what matters. The writer does.
fragment: The system doesn't decide what matters
where: The first appearance of "mirror, not oracle."
why: A tool that guesses what's important takes the work away from the person doing it.

rule: Two things with different labels aren't the same thing.
quote: Sparks and Etches are not tags with different labels.
fragment: are not tags with different labels
where: Separating Sparks from Etches.
why: If two things behave differently, a shared shape will hurt both of them.

rule: Some of your best features are accidents you keep.
quote: In the Spark creation modal, I had accidentally included the ability to tie a Spark to a wiki page.
fragment: I had accidentally included the ability to tie a Spark to a wiki page
where: An accidental Spark-to-wiki-page link that became a POV timeline I never designed.
why: Watching what a mistake makes possible can show you what people actually want.

rule: When everything is connected, new capabilities emerge on their own.
quote: This is what a graph gives you. When everything is connected, new capabilities don't require new architecture.
fragment: new capabilities don't require new architecture
where: Features that fell out of the graph without new building.
why: Good connections pay for themselves more than once.

rule: The holes in your product are the shape of your own workflow.
quote: The holes were the shape of my workflow.
fragment: The holes were the shape of my workflow
where: The first outside writers finding gaps I'd never hit.
why: You only test the paths you walk yourself.

rule: Building for other people is where the product starts.
quote: The product stopped being something I was building in my room and became something I was building for other people.
fragment: something I was building for other people
where: Opening the app to others.
why: A tool only one person uses hasn't been tested yet.

rule: Expect to be wrong.
quote: Every month since the inception, I have been wrong about something.
fragment: I have been wrong about something
where: Looking back over the first five months.
why: Planning for it makes the next correction cheaper.

rule: Don't design systems at 3 a.m.
quote: Don't design systems at 3 a.m.
fragment: design systems at 3
where: The sync design I threw out.
why: Decisions made tired cost more to undo than they saved.

rule: It's better to show nothing for two seconds than a lie for half a second.
quote: It is better to show nothing for two seconds than to show a lie for half a second.
fragment: better to show nothing for two seconds
where: Optimistic updates that showed the wrong state.
why: A wrong screen breaks trust faster than a slow one.

rule: Give things a real identity from the start.
quote: Instead of a temporary name that gets rewritten, the client generates a UUIDv7 before the mutation ever runs.
fragment: the client generates a UUIDv7
where: Replacing temporary ids with UUIDv7.
why: Anything that gets renamed later gives the system a chance to lose track of it.

rule: The hard road is empty for a reason.
fragment: The hard road is empty for a reason
where: Building the Word import myself.
why: If nobody else has done it, find out why before you start.

rule: A promise of perfection is a commitment to lie.
fragment: A promise of perfection is a commitment to lie
where: Deciding what the import could honestly promise.
why: Saying what you can't do is part of being trusted.

rule: Formatting tells you how someone wrote, not what they meant.
quote: Word doesn't tell you what the writer meant. It tells you how the writer formatted, and you work backward.
fragment: Word doesn't tell you what the writer meant
where: Inferring chapters and scenes from Word formatting.
why: The surface is evidence, not the answer.

rule: To an agent, "done" is a state. It isn't the same thing as correct.
fragment: To an agent, "done" is a state. It isn't the same thing as correct
where: The Scene Designer save that reported success and wasn't.

rule: Understand your problem before you take generic advice.
fragment: Understand your problem before you take generic advice
where: Generic testing advice that didn't fit aampersand.

rule: Be very clear about what you're actually testing.
fragment: Be very clear about what you're actually testing
where: The tests that checked the mocks, not the app.

rule: A test may pass but still fail to test its target.
fragment: A test may pass but still fail to test its target
where: Checking that the original passages, scenes and notes stay untouched.

rule: Iteration is the learning.
fragment: Iteration is the learning
where: Deleting the test suite in October and starting again.
